title: Injectivity of the Configuration Encoding
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, and let $n,s,C\in\mathbb N$ with $C\ge |Q|+6k+5$, where $Q$ is its state set. For any Boolean input $x$ of length $n$ and configurations $c,d$ on $x$ whose work-tape heads lie within distance $s$ of the origin and whose work tapes are blank outside that interval, their configuration encodings are equal exactly when their states, input-head positions, work-tape contents, work-tape head positions, and output summaries are all equal.
hypotheses_covered: M is a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols
n, s, and C are natural numbers
C is at least the number of states of M plus 6k+5
x is a Boolean input of length n
c and d are configurations of M on x
each work-tape head position of c and d has absolute value at most s
each work tape of c and d is blank at every cell whose absolute position exceeds s
